      Reading comprehension

      The worksheet bank

      Three reading folders, 20 sheets in each, plus sheets for the hand and number activities (Letter Heights, Fingers and Dice, Count and Circle, Play-Doh Take-Away and the life-size Hand Positions pages). Every school day uses one word family sheet and one comprehension sheet. Each month takes the next sheets in each folder, so a sheet only comes back once the whole folder has been used, or on purpose on a review day.

      Addition flashcards

      The 65-fact bank

      Every fact with a first number from 0 to 9 and an answer of 10 or less. Waves follow the school days of the month: days 1–5 are Wave 1, days 6–10 Wave 2, days 11–15 Wave 3, and days 16 onward mix all 65 facts.

      Wave 1: 0, 1, 2 + ___ (30 facts) Wave 2: 3, 4, 5 + ___ (21 facts) Wave 3: 6, 7, 8, 9 + ___ (14 facts)
      ASL

      99 signs, nine at a time

      Alissa's ASL list is split into 11 sets of nine, in the list's own order, starting from the sign she began with (What, on September 25). After sign 99 the list wraps back to sign 1. Each school day uses five signs from the set. Over the set's nine school days, every sign is practiced exactly 5 times, and no sign ever goes more than one day without practice. Signs 1–5 are taught on day 1, and signs 6–9 come in one a day on days 2–5, so each gets a day as the newcomer. A new sign is always practiced again the next day. After nine school days the next set begins. This count runs straight through month ends. Always check a sign against its video before teaching it.

      This set, day by day

      A filled square means the sign is practiced that day, and “N” marks its newcomer day. Tap a day number to see that day's five signs, or tap a sign for its description and video.

      How we run it

      Supporting Alissa

      Alissa is 12 and autistic, and she's working at about a first-grade level. The plan keeps the work at her level and treats her like the 12-year-old she is.

      Predictable days

      • Same order every day, High Tide or Low Tide. Only the games change.
      • Walk through the schedule together at the start. Tick each block as it finishes so she can see how much is done.
      • Start the timer for each block so she can see how long is left. The bar turns coral with 2 minutes to go. Say that warning out loud too.
      • If a change is coming, such as a new game or a switch to Low Tide, tell her before the block starts.

      Clear, calm communication

      • One direction at a time, in plain words. Show it as well as saying it.
      • Wait 5–10 seconds after a question before helping.
      • Offer two choices instead of open questions: “Crab walk or wall push-ups?”
      • Use First/Then: “First reading, then snack.”

      Body and senses

      • Heavy-work moves (wall push-ups, carrying books) help her settle. Use them before sitting work.
      • Keep music low and use a countdown (“3, 2, 1, freeze”) so nothing stops suddenly. Have headphones ready.
      • Any game can be done in a smaller way: tapping instead of hopping, sitting instead of standing.
      • Competition is always against her own score, never against someone else.

      On hard days

      • Do the arrival check-in at the top of today's schedule. Shelly suggests a tide from it and the last few sessions.
      • Short work bursts toward what she picked on her token board.
      • Every time she asks for a break (✋ button, card, sign or words), give it right away and count it.
      • After Spit, Hit or Refused, tap what happened right before. Shelly's support plan has the full research-based steps.

      Kit we use

      • Painter's tape (number line 0–10, hopscotch, answer letters)
      • Index cards and a marker
      • A squishy toy and a soft ball
      • Counters or blocks for math
      • Highlighters and colored pencils for worksheets
      • Headphones and a quiet corner
      • The Item checklist on each day lists exactly what that day needs.
      “Print worksheets and cards” makes one PDF with that day's worksheets and every card set the day uses. Cards are laid out to be cut in order, in up to three stacks marked with a star, a circle and a triangle so each stack fits the paper cutter: cut each stack on its own, then put the star cards first, circle next and triangle last. Edits to the plan are saved for everyone who opens this page. Done ticks are shared with every device; the timer and its settings stay on each device. “Print schedule” makes a PDF of just the schedule. Every PDF opens as a preview first.

        Privacy notice full details
        What this page keeps
        • Session records: which tasks were done, her results (words, addition facts, signs, worksheet marks), star ratings, behavior counts and Wendy's session notes and progress log answers.
        • The schedule and plans: session times, moved or skipped days, reading and addition plans, and settings.
        • Summaries and notes Claude wrote when you asked for them, and Shelly's recent activity.
        Why

        Only to plan Alissa's tutoring, see what is working, and share progress with her family. Nothing is sold or used for advertising.

        Where it is stored

        In this page's own database on claude.ai, run by Anthropic under its own privacy policy. Deleting the page deletes its database too.

        Who can see it

        Anyone who can open this page can see her records, and people with editing access can change them. The page link can be shared, so share it only with her family and team, and never post it publicly. Family members who open the link see the read-only recap view.

        What is sent to Claude

        When you ask for a summary, a chart explanation, Shelly's ideas or polished notes, the page sends the session details that question needs (counts, ratings and notes) to Claude, Anthropic's AI, to write the answer. It uses her first name only, never her surname. The answers are saved here as summaries.

        Other services

        Fonts load from Google Fonts and the PDF tools from cdnjs (Cloudflare). Like any website, loading them shares your device's internet address and browser type with those services. No session data is sent to them.

        Storage in this browser

        This browser remembers your preferences (theme, sounds, timer, view) and keeps a quick copy of a few things, such as done tasks and Shelly's recent activity, so the page loads fast. If the database can't be reached, a session is saved on this device only. There is no tracking, analytics or advertising and no cookies are set, so no cookie banner is needed.

        How long it is kept

        Records stay until you delete them. You can download everything or delete all session records above at any time, and you can ask Wendy to correct or remove anything.

        Terms of use
        • This is a private educational planning tool for Alissa's tutoring, used by her tutor and family.
        • It is not medical, clinical or therapy advice, and it doesn't diagnose anything.
        • The support plan and Shelly's suggestions are general guidance drawn from published educational practices. Decisions about her care belong with her family, doctor, BCBA and school team.
        • Activity descriptions say what each activity is meant to practise; every child responds differently.
        • Claude's summaries can be wrong. Check them against your own notes.
        • Please don't share the link publicly or copy her records elsewhere without her family's okay.
